Ophthalmology is a specialised service industry; availability and retention of qualified ophthalmologists, doctors, nurses and paramedical personnel are critical to operations, and specialised ophthalmologists and trained paramedical personnel are in limited supply industry-wide.

Healthcare operations are governed by various statutory, regulatory and professional requirements; changes in applicable laws, regulations, standards or healthcare policies may affect operations and costs.
Rapid developments in ophthalmic technology require continuous evaluation and investment in medical equipment and training.
Rising costs of medical equipment, consumables, manpower and other operating inputs may put pressure on margins.
Cyber security risks were flagged among factors that may affect operating costs and profitability, alongside rising equipment, consumables and manpower costs and pricing pressures.

risks.body:

- Healthcare operations are governed by various statutory, regulatory and professional requirements; changes in applicable laws, regulations, standards or healthcare policies may affect operations and costs.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Strengthen clinical capabilities, adopt relevant technologies, improve operational efficiency and expand reach.
- Continue to expand into emerging and underserved markets by taking quality eye care closer to patients.
- Continue to evaluate and adopt appropriate technologies (advanced diagnostics, digital healthcare) while maintaining prudent financial discipline.
- Focus on recruitment, professional development, training and retention of skilled ophthalmology personnel.
